X.finding: Model APPROVE triggers payment with model-extracted amount, no adjuster
X.why: TriageService.java:66-67 calls payments.pay with result.amountClaimed()/currency() when autoApprove, and application.yml:9 sets auto-approve: true; the report names the unchecked amount and the missing human.

X.finding: Repeat POST of the same claimId pays twice (no idempotency)
X.why: ClaimsController.java:27-31 re-runs triage on every POST and PaymentService.java:20-22 appends each payment without checking for an existing claimId, so a retried request creates a second payment.

X.finding: Claimant email concatenated into the system prompt (prompt injection)
X.why: TriageService.java:41 appends email to the prompt and :51 passes it as .system(prompt); the report says an email can make the model return APPROVE with its own amount, i.e. pay itself out.

X.finding: Summary page builds HTML from model summary and claimId without escaping (XSS)
X.why: ClaimsController.java:35 serves text/html and :39/:41 concatenate claimId and r.summary() unescaped; the report names both the model-output and reflected path-variable vectors.

X.finding: Production-looking API key committed in application.yml
X.why: application.yml:7 holds api-key: claims-prod-9f2c4e1a7b3d8e60, injected at TriageService.java:27; the report says the key is in the repo and should come from the environment.

X.finding: temperature(0.0) makes Haiku 5.5 reject every call with a 400
X.why: TriageService.java:50 sets temperature(0.0) and application.yml:6 selects claude-haiku-5-5; the report states that this model returns a 400 for a non-default temperature, so all 5 attempts fail.

X.finding: Content read before checking stopReason (refusal / max_tokens truncation)
X.why: TriageService.java:55 reads content().get(0).text().get() with no stopReason() check; the report names both the refusal and the max_tokens cut-off cases and the refusal being retried.

X.finding: Claim email, model answer and SDK error messages logged
X.why: TriageService.java:56 logs prompt (containing the email) and answer at INFO, and :59 logs e.getMessage(); the report names both lines and the personal data.

X.finding: Client built per attempt, 5-attempt loop on top of SDK retries, no timeout
X.why: TriageService.java:46 builds a new AnthropicOkHttpClient inside the :44 loop with no timeout; the report names the per-request client and the stacked retries (both halves).

X.finding: catch (Exception) retries everything and discards the cause
X.why: TriageService.java:58-59 catches every Exception, logs only getMessage() and retries non-retryable errors (bad key, parse errors); the final IllegalStateException at :63 carries no cause.

X.finding: Triage failure surfaces as 500 instead of 503 with Retry-After
X.why: TriageService.java:63 throws IllegalStateException, which Spring maps to 500; preferring 503 + Retry-After is a checklist convention rather than a defect the code demonstrates.

X.finding: No validation or size bound on the claim email sent to the model
X.why: ClaimsController.java:18 ClaimRequest(String email) has no @NotBlank/@Size and :28 has no @Valid; the report says a 5 MB email goes to the model at the operator's cost, and a missing email becomes "null" in the prompt (TriageService.java:41).
TriageResult.java:4 amountClaimed is double and PaymentService.java:16/:20 pass double amount; the report names the rounding problem and BigDecimal-style fix.

X.finding: Triage results stored in the controller rather than behind the service
X.why: ClaimsController.java:21 holds a ConcurrentHashMap of results; layering preference, and the in-memory map is on the key's Not-defects list.
There is no src/test; the key lists 'no tests' as a Not-defect.

X.finding: No authentication on triage and adjuster summary endpoints
X.why: ClaimsController.java:27 and :35 are open (no Spring Security in pom.xml:17-21), so anyone can trigger triage, and with auto-approve a payment, or read another claimant's summary.
